scenario: A global space camp shortlists candidates if they have either elite coding skill or elite navigation skill. A 10% wildcard also admits candidates with neither trait. Analysts see a negative association between coding and navigation among finalists.

data.description: Finalist selection is based on either of two strengths, plus a wildcard from the neither group.

question: Among finalists, compute (a) P(coding | navigation, finalist), and (b) P(coding | not navigation, finalist). Is the apparent negative association real or induced by selection?

ground_truth.explanation: Coding and navigation are independent in the population. The finalist rule creates the negative association.

naive_answer: Among finalists, coding and navigation look negatively related, so the skills probably substitute for each other.
naive_trap: This is collider bias from shortlisting on either skill.
